messages:
maya: heads up — we need to settle on an envelope encryption pattern for multi-cloud KMS: AWS KMS + GCP KMS + Azure Key Vault. DEK/KEK separation is obvious, but looking for guidance on cache TTLs and rotation semantics.

sam: for context, traffic is bursty, so we can't call KMS on every request. current idea: cache DEKs in memory per host with a short TTL + subscribe to revocation events. :thinking: 

jordan: agree on DEK caching per-host. keep KEK calls only for wrap/unwrap at DEK creation or rotation. i.e., generate DEK locally (CSPRNG), then call KMS.Encrypt(KEK, DEK) once and store wrapped_DEK. unwrap only on restart or when cache miss.

maya: that makes sense. questions: 1) TTL length? 2) how to handle cross-region/cross-cloud revokes? 3) audit logging for unwrap ops (sensitive)

eli: compliance asks that every KEK unwrap/Encrypt call is logged with principal, key version, and purpose. if we cache DEKs long-lived we need compensating controls (short TTLs + attestation).

sam: proposed defaults: in-memory DEK TTL = 5m for low-latency paths, 0s for high-security tenants (configurable per-tenant). also add LRU cap (~1000 DEKs) to bound memory.

jordan: we should encode metadata with wrapped_DEK: {kms_provider, key_id, key_version, created_at, expire_at}. on unwrap, validate key_version still active. store it as JSON next to wrapped blob.

maya: for revocation propagation, we can rely on: 1) KMS key rotation events (cloud pubsub/webhooks) 2) periodic reconcile job that lists key versions 3) short TTL to limit window. which of these are feasible?

sam: all three. AWS has CloudWatch Events for key rotation and grants changes, GCP has Pub/Sub notifications for CMEK changes if we hook it, Azure has Event Grid. ops-bot can subscribe.

ops-bot: rotation: scheduled job created. next-run: 2026-03-25T02:00:00Z. will emit events to #eng-security and trigger cache invalidation webhook. :white_check_mark:

jordan: design note: avoid calling KMS for every cache invalidation. instead send a short invalidation message (key_id + new_version) to all hosts; hosts then evict DEKs whose key_version != current. reduces calls to KMS.

maya: what about DEK re-encryption on KEK rotation? do we rewrap all stored DEKs immediately or lazily on use?

eli: auditors prefer proactive rewrap within SLAs. but for large fleets, lazy rewrap on first use + background rewrap queue with exponential backoff is acceptable if documented.

sam: implementation plan: - generate DEK per object/tenant - wrap with KMS.Encrypt -> store wrapped_DEK + metadata - cache unwrapped DEK in memory TTL 5m - on cache miss, call KMS.Decrypt once and serve - background rewrap job to re-encrypt wrapped_DEKs to newest KEK version asynchronously

jordan: snippet for wrap/unwrap pseudo: 
```
// create
dek = random_bytes(32)
wrapped = KMS.Encrypt(kek_id, dek)
store({wrapped_blob: wrapped, meta: {kek_id, version}})

// load
record = lookup(id)
if cache.has(record.id) return cache.get(record.id)
dek = KMS.Decrypt(record.meta.kek_id, record.wrapped_blob)
cache.set(record.id, dek, ttl=5m)
return dek
```

maya: edge case: if KMS.Decrypt fails due to permission denied (policy change) we should fail safe and surface clear audit events. do not auto-fallback to older KEK without an explicit policy.

eli: RBAC change: we must ensure service principals used for unwrap have narrow permissions and that keys have grants scoped to environment/tenant. log the principal used per-call.

jordan: cross-cloud nuance: Azure returns different error codes for revoked keys vs unknown key. normalize error handling in client lib so callers see consistent enums (REVOKED, NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION).

sam: caching strategy summary: per-host memory cache, TTL 5m default, configurable per-tenant, LRU cap, invalidation via event bus. unwrap calls only on cache miss or rewrap ops. KEK rotation handled lazily plus background rewrap; auditors get proactive job if requested.

maya: follow-ups: 1) prototype client lib with normalized errors and metadata support 2) ops-bot to wire KMS events to internal bus 3) add audit schema for unwrap/wrap ops and record key_version + principal + request_id. i'll file tickets.

ops-bot: ticket created: SEC-1204 "Envelope encryption: DEK cache and rotation plan" assigned to maya/sam/jordan. due: 2026-04-08.

sam: thanks — i'll sketch the library API tomorrow. anyone object to the TTL defaults?

jordan: fine from platform side. we should expose config flags for tenants with strict compliance.

eli: approved for compliance with the listed compensating controls.

maya: great, closing this thread unless anything else. :shield:
